F- 47 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 1- ORGANIZATION Conwall Construction Industries Limited (the “Company” or “Conwall”) was incorporated on February 12, 2026, under the laws of the Cayman Islands as an exempted company. Conwall was incorporated as a holding company for the purpose of acquiring operating companies. On July 16, 2026, the Company completed the share exchange described below and became the holding company of Conwall Construction Industries Sdn. Bhd. On July 16, 2026, the Company entered into a Share Swap Agreement (the “Share Swap Agreement”) with the shareholders holding all 750,000 issued and outstanding ordinary shares of Conwall Construction Industries Sdn. Bhd. (“Conwall Malaysia”). Conwall Malaysia was incorporated in Malaysia on October 8, 2019, as a private company limited by shares under the Companies Act 2016 and is engaged in the business of providing construction and maintenance services. Pursuant to the Share Swap Agreement, the Company issued an aggregate of 30,000,000 shares of its common stock to the shareholders of Conwall Malaysia in exchange for all of the issued and outstanding ordinary shares of Conwall Malaysia. Specifically, the Company issued 21,000,000 shares of its common stock to Mr. Ng Boon Teik in exchange for his 525,000 ordinary shares of Conwall Malaysia, and 9,000,000 shares of its common stock to Mr. Hu Jingji in exchange for his 225,000 ordinary shares of Conwall Malaysia. Upon completion of the share exchange, Conwall Malaysia became a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company. The share exchanges have been accounted for as a recapitalization of entities under common control because the same controlling shareholders controlled both entities before and after the transaction. Accordingly, the consolidation of the Company and its subsidiary has been accounted for at historical cost, and the accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared as if the transaction had occurred at the beginning of the earliest period presented. The Company, through its wholly owned subsidiary, Conwall Malaysia, is engaged in the business of providing construction and maintenance services. The Company and its subsidiary are collectively referred to as the “Group” or the “Company”. Where appropriate, the terms “we,” “our,” and “us” refer collectively to Conwall and its subsidiary. Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES Basis of Presentation and Principles of Consolidation The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”) and pursuant to the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”). The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its subsidiaries. All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated. F- 48 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Foreign Currency Translation The accompanying consolidated financial statements are presented in United States dollar (“USD”), which is the reporting currency of the Company. The functional currency of Conwall is USD. The functional currency of Conwall Malaysia is Malaysian Ringgit (“MYR”). The Company maintains the books and record in the functional currency. Transactions denominated in currencies other than the functional currency are translated into the functional currency at the exchange rates prevailing at the dates of the transaction. The resulting exchange differences are recorded in the statements of operations. The reporting currency of the Company is the United States Dollars (“USD”), and the accompanying consolidated financial statements have been expressed in USD. In accordance with ASC Topic 830-30, “Translation of Financial Statements”, assets and liabilities of the Company whose functional currency is not US$ are translated into USD, using the exchange rate on the balance sheet date. Revenues and expenses are translated at average rates prevailing during the period. The gains and losses resulting from the translation of financial statements are recorded as a separate component of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) within the statements of changes in shareholders’ equity (deficit). The exchange rates used for foreign currency translation were as follows: SCHEDULE OF EXCHANGE RATES USED FOR FOREIGN CURRENCY TRANSLATION USD$1 = MYR Period Covered Balance Sheet Date Rates Average Rates Year ended March 31, 2026 4.4365 4.5067 Year ended March 31, 2025 4.7225 4.6409 Statements of Cash Flows In accordance with FASB ASC 830-230, “Statement of Cash Flows”, cash flows from the Company’s operations is calculated based upon the functional currency. As a result, amounts related to assets and liabilities reported on the statement of cash flows may not necessarily agree with changes in the corresponding balances on the balance sheet. F- 49 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Use of Estimates The preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect reported amounts. These estimates are based on information available through the date of the issuance of the financial statements. Therefore, actual results could differ from those estimates. Fair Value of Financial Instruments The Company adopted ASC 820 “Fair Value Measurements,” which defines fair value, establishes a three-level valuation hierarchy for disclosures of fair value measurement and enhances disclosures requirements for fair value measures. Current assets and current liabilities qualified as financial instruments and management believes their carrying amounts are a reasonable estimate of fair value because of the short period of time between the origination of such instruments and their expected realization and if applicable, their current interest rate is equivalent to interest rates currently available. The three levels are defined as follow: Level 1: Inputs to the valuation methodology are quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets. Level 2: Inputs to the valuation methodology include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs that are observable for the assets or liability, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the financial instruments. Level 3: Inputs to the valuation methodology are unobservable and significant to the fair value. As of the balance sheet date, the estimated fair values of the financial instruments approximated their fair values due to the short-term nature of these instruments. Determining which category an asset or liability falls within the hierarchy requires significant judgment. The Company evaluates the hierarchy disclosures each year. Cash and Cash Equivalents Cash and cash equivalents include cash on hand and cash in time deposits, certificates of deposit and all other highly liquid instruments with original maturities of three months or less. Restricted Fixed Deposits Certain customers occasionally require the Company to place fixed deposits with licensed financial institutions as security deposits to guarantee the completion of construction projects. The Company places such fixed deposits with reputable banks for terms generally ranging from six to twelve months. These deposits are typically withdrawn upon completion of the related construction projects or upon customer approval. At that time, the principal and accrued interest are released to the Company and become available for working capital purposes. The Company recognizes interest income on these fixed deposits over the term of the deposit. F- 50 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Accounts Receivable, net Accounts receivable, net represent amounts for which the Company has an unconditional right to consideration and are stated at the invoiced amount, net of an allowance for expected credit losses. The Company evaluates the collectability of its accounts receivable on a recurring basis and maintains adequate allowance for expected credit losses based on management’s estimate of lifetime expected credit losses. In estimating the allowance, the Company considers historical collection experience, the aging of receivable balances, customers’ financial condition and creditworthiness, current economic conditions, reasonable and supportable forecasts, and other relevant factors that may affect customers’ ability to pay. Accounts receivable are written off against the allowance when management determines that collection is not probable. Subsequent recoveries of amounts previously written off are recorded by reversing the allowance and reducing bad debt expense in the period received. Advance Payments Advance payments represent amounts paid to material suppliers and subcontractors in accordance with the terms of purchase contracts and subcontract agreements. These payments are applied against future billings from the respective suppliers and subcontractors as materials are delivered or services are performed. Advance payments are classified as current or non-current assets based on the Company’s expectation of when the related goods or services will be received and the advances will be applied. Amounts expected to be applied within one year after the balance sheet date are classified as current assets, while amounts expected to be applied after one year are classified as non-current assets. Project Retention Project retention represents the portion of the contract price withheld by customers from progress payments on completed construction projects. These retentions serve as security for the satisfactory performance of the Company’s contractual obligations, including any defects or warranty claims. Retained amounts are generally released to the Company in accordance with the terms of the respective contracts, typically within one to two years after project completion upon the expiry of the warranty or defect liability period. Project retentions are classified as current or non-current, depending on the expected release date, and are stated at their original amount less any allowance for doubtful accounts, if required. The Company periodically reviews the collectability of project retentions and recognizes an allowance when there is objective evidence that the amounts may not be fully recoverable. Write-offs and recoveries are accounted for in the same manner as accounts receivable. F- 51 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Property, plant and equipment Property and equipment primarily consist of office renovation and furniture, and office equipment, which are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation, and less any provision required for impairment in value. Depreciation is computed using the straight-line method based on the estimated useful lives as follows: SCHEDULE OF PROPERTY, PLANT AND EQUIPMENT ESTIMATED USEFUL LIVEs Office furniture 10 years Office equipment 2.5 years Leasehold improvements 5 years or lease term, whichever is shorter Costs of repairs and maintenance are expensed as incurred and asset improvements are capitalized. The cost and related accumulated depreciation of assets disposed of or retired are removed from the accounts, and any resulting gain or loss is reflected in the consolidated statement of operations and comprehensive income. Refundable Insurance Premium On August 7, 2025, the Company purchased a five-year key person life insurance policy covering one of its executive officers. The policy provides a death benefit of $ 370,627 (RM 1,500,000 ) and a total and permanent disability benefit of $ 370,627 (RM 1,500,000 ) through August 6, 2030. The Company paid a single premium of $ 247,161 (RM 1,000,311 ) (exclusive of applicable taxes) upon issuance of the policy. The premium was financed through a bank loan, with the loan proceeds disbursed directly by the lending institution to the insurer, as more fully disclosed in Note 11 – Bank Loan – Fixed Loan. The policy does not provide any cash surrender value during its five-year coverage term. Under the terms of the policy, if no death or total and permanent disability claim is made during the coverage period and the policy remains in force through its maturity date, the insurer is contractually obligated to refund 100% of the single premium paid to the Company upon maturity. Because the policy has no cash surrender value and the premium is contractually refundable only upon maturity, the Company records the refundable premium as a noncurrent asset in the consolidated balance sheets. The Company evaluates the recoverability of this asset at each reporting date and records an allowance for credit losses or impairment when collection of the refundable premium is no longer considered probable. The Company does not recognize the $ 370,627 (RM 1,500,000 ) death benefit or total and permanent disability benefit as an asset because the receipt of such benefits is contingent upon future insured events. Any proceeds received under the policy in excess of the carrying amount of the refundable premium will be recognized in earnings when realized. Impairment of long-lived assets The Company reviews long-lived assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable. Recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset to the future undiscounted cash flows expected to be generated by the asset. If such assets are considered to be impaired, the impairment recognized is measured by the amount by which the carrying amount of the assets exceeds the fair value of the assets. No impairment of long-lived assets was recognized for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025. F- 52 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Project Security Deposits Project security deposits represent amounts received from subcontractors as security for the satisfactory performance of their contractual obligations. These deposits are refundable upon the completion of the related projects and the expiration of the applicable warranty period, provided the subcontractors have fulfilled all contractual requirements. Project security deposits are classified as current or non-current liabilities based on the Company’s expectation of when the related deposits will become refundable. Deposits expected to be refunded within one year after the balance sheet date are classified as current liabilities, while those expected to be refunded after one year are classified as non-current liabilities. Lease The Company leases are classified as operating leases in accordance with Topic 842. Under Topic 842, lessees are required to recognize the following for all leases (with the exception of short-term leases) on the commencement date: (i) lease liability, which is a lessee’s obligation to make lease payments arising from a lease, measured on a discounted basis; and (ii) right-of-use asset, which is an asset that represents the lessee’s right to use, or control the use of, a specified asset for the lease term. At the commencement date, the Company recognizes the lease liability at the present value of the lease payments not yet paid, discounted using the interest rate implicit in the lease or, if that rate cannot be readily determined, the Company’s incremental borrowing rate for the same term as the underlying lease. The right-of-use asset is recognized initially at cost, which primarily comprises the initial amount of the lease liability, plus any initial direct costs incurred, consisting mainly of brokerage commissions, less any lease incentives received. All right-of-use assets are reviewed for impairment. No impairment for right-of-use lease assets incurred in the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025. Concentration of Credit Risk Financial instruments the Company holds that are subject to concentrations of credit risk are cash and accounts receivable arising from its normal business activities. The Company maintains cash balances with high-credit-quality financial institutions that periodically exceed insured limits. As of March 31, 2026 and 2025, substantially all of the Company’s cash deposits were held with financial institutions in Malaysia, and certain balances exceeded the applicable deposit insurance limits. Management regularly monitors the creditworthiness of these institutions. The Company has not experienced any losses on such deposits and believes it is not exposed to any significant credit risk on its cash balances. For the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, two customers and four customers, respectively, accounted for more than 10% of the Company’s total sales. For the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, two vendors and one vendor, respectively, accounted for more than 10% of the Company’s total purchases. F- 53 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Revenue Recognition The Company adopted ASC 606 upon inception. Under ASC 606, revenue is recognized when a customer obtains control of promised goods or services, in an amount that reflects the consideration which the entity expects to receive in exchange for those goods or services. To determine revenue recognition for arrangements that an entity determines are within the scope of ASC 606, the Company performs the following five steps: (i) identify the contract(s) with a customer; (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract; (iii) determine the transaction price; (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation. The Company derives its revenue primarily from construction contracts with customers. Revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606 when control of the promised goods or services is transferred to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration the Company expects to receive in exchange for those goods or services. Construction contracts generally contain a single performance obligation because the individual services provided under the contract are not separately identifiable and are integrated into a single combined output, which is the completed construction project. Revenue from construction contracts is recognized over time, as the Company’s performance creates or enhances an asset that the customer controls as the asset is constructed. Progress toward completion is measured using the cost-to-cost input method, under which the percentage of completion is determined by comparing costs incurred to date with total estimated contract costs. Revenue recognized to date is calculated by applying the percentage of completion to the total transaction price of the contract. Revenue recognized in the current period represents the cumulative revenue recognized to date less amounts recognized in prior periods. Costs incurred include direct materials, direct labor, subcontractor costs, and other costs directly attributable to the contract. Management periodically reviews and updates estimates of total contract costs. Changes in estimated costs or contract value are recognized as cumulative catch-up adjustments to revenue in the period the estimates change. Timing differences between revenue recognized and amounts billed to customers result in contract assets or contract liabilities. A contract asset is recorded when revenue recognized exceeds billings to the customer, while a contract liability is recorded when billings exceed revenue recognized. The Company expects substantially all contract assets outstanding as of March 31, 2026 to be billed and collected within one year. The Company also expects substantially all contract liabilities outstanding as of March 31, 2026 to be recognized as revenue within one year. If at any time the estimated total costs of a contract exceed the transaction price, the Company recognizes the entire estimated loss immediately in the period in which the loss becomes probable. F- 54 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Revenue Recognition (continued) For certain sundry construction projects with a total contract price of less than $ 24,020 (RM 100,000 ) or an expected duration of less than three months , the Company does not apply the cost-to-cost input method to measure progress toward completion. Due to the short-term nature and immaterial size of these contracts, revenue is recognized by matching revenue with the related costs incurred within the same reporting period. Management has concluded that this approach does not result in a material difference from the revenue that would have been recognized using the cost-to-cost input method. The Company generally provides limited warranties for work performed under its contracts. These warranties are assurance-type warranties that provide customers with assurance that the completed work complies with agreed-upon specifications and do not represent separate performance obligations. Historically, warranty claims have not resulted in material costs incurred. Any estimated warranty costs are included in the individual project cost estimates used in accounting for long-term contracts. Project Estimates Due to the nature of our industry, there is significant complexity in our estimation of total expected revenue and cost, for which we must make significant judgments. Our contracts with our customers may contain several types of variable consideration, including claims, unpriced change orders, award and incentive fees, liquidated damages and penalties or other provisions that can either increase or decrease the contract price to arrive at estimated revenue. Certain variable consideration, such as award and incentive fees, generally are earned upon achievement of certain performance metrics, program milestones or cost targets and can be based upon customer discretion. We estimate variable consideration at the most likely amount to which we expect to be entitled upon completion of a project. We include estimated amounts in the transaction price to the extent it is probable we will realize that amount. Our estimates of variable consideration and our determination of its inclusion in project revenue are based on an assessment of our anticipated performance and other information that may be available to us. At a project level, we have specific practices and procedures to review our estimate of total revenue and cost. Each project team reviews the progress and execution of our performance obligations, which impact the project’s accounting outcome. As part of this process, the project team reviews information such as any outstanding key contract matters, progress towards completion and the related program schedule and identified risks and opportunities. The accuracy of our revenue and profit recognition in a given period depends on the accuracy of our project estimates, which can change from period to period due to a variety of factors including: ● Complexity in original design; ● Extent of changes from original design; ● Different site conditions than assumed in our bid; ● Length of time to complete the project; ● Availability and cost of equipment and materials; ● Subcontractor performance; ● Our ability to recover for additional contract costs. We recognize changes in contract estimates on a cumulative catch-up basis in the period in which the changes are identified. Such changes in contract estimates can result in the recognition of revenue in a current period for performance obligations which were satisfied or partially satisfied in prior periods. Changes in contract estimates may also result in the reversal of previously recognized revenue if the current estimate adversely differs from the previous estimate. F- 55 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Remaining Performance Obligations The Company’s remaining performance obligations as of March 31, 2026 represent a measure of the total dollar value of work to be performed on contracts awarded and in progress. The Company had approximately $ 18,062,490 in remaining performance obligations as of March 31, 2026. The Company expects to recognize 100% of our remaining performance obligations within the next twelve months . Although remaining performance obligations reflect business that is considered to be firm, cancellations, scope adjustments, foreign currency exchange fluctuations or project deferrals may occur that impact their volume or the expected timing of their recognition. Remaining performance obligations are adjusted to reflect any known project. Comprehensive Income (Loss) ASC 220 “Comprehensive Income” established standards for reporting and display of comprehensive income/loss, its components and accumulated balances. Components of comprehensive income/loss include net income/loss and foreign currency translation adjustments. The component of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) consisted of foreign currency translation adjustments. Earnings per share Basic earnings per ordinary share is computed by dividing net earnings attributable to ordinary shareholders by the weighted-average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the period. Diluted earnings per share is computed by dividing net income attributable to ordinary shareholders by the sum of the weighted average number of ordinary share outstanding and of potential ordinary share (e.g., convertible securities, options and warrants) as if they had been converted at the beginning of the periods presented, or issuance date, if later. Potential ordinary shares that have an anti-dilutive effect (i.e., those that increase income per share or decrease loss per share) are excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share. For the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company had no dilutive stocks. Segment Reporting ASC 280, “Segment Reporting,” requires use of the “management approach” model for segment reporting. The management approach model is based on the way a company’s chief operating decision maker organizes segments within the Company for making operating decisions assessing performance and allocating resources. Reportable segments are based on products and services, geography, legal structure, management structure, or any other manner in which management disaggregates a company. Management determined the Company’s operations constitute one reportable segment in accordance with ASC 280, construction and maintenance services. F- 56 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Income Taxes The Company accounts for current income taxes in accordance with the laws of the relevant tax authorities. Deferred income taxes are recognized when temporary differences exist between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their reported amounts in the consolidated financial statements. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period including the enactment date. Valuation allowances are established, when necessary, to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized. An uncertain tax position is recognized only if it is “more likely than not” that the tax position would be sustained in a tax examination. The amount recognized is the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50% likely of being realized on examination. For tax positions not meeting the “more likely than not” test, no tax benefit is recorded. Penalties and interest incurred related to underpayment of income tax are classified as income tax expense in the period incurred. (1) Income tax of Cayman Islands Conwall was incorporated in the Cayman Islands as an exempted company and is governed by the tax laws of the Cayman Islands. Under the current laws of the Cayman Islands, Conwall is not subject to income taxes or capital gains taxes. In addition, upon payment of dividends by Conwall to its shareholders, no Cayman Islands withholding tax will be imposed. (2) Income tax of Malaysia Conwall Malaysia was incorporated in Malaysia, and accordingly are governed by the income tax laws of Malaysia. The income tax provision in respect of operations in Malaysia is calculated at the applicable tax rates on the taxable income for the periods based on existing legislation, interpretations, and practices. Under the Income Tax Act of Malaysia, enterprises incorporated in Malaysia are usually subject to a unified 24 % enterprise income tax rate while prefer, tax holidays, and tax exemptions may be granted on a case-by-case basis. The tax rate for small and medium sized companies (generally companies incorporated in Malaysia with paid-in capital of $617,711 (RM2,500,000) or less, and gross income of not more than $12,010,280 (RM50,000,000) is 15% on the first $36,030 (RM150,000) of taxable income and 17% on taxable income from $36,031 (RM150,001) to $144,123 (RM600,000), with any remaining taxable income taxed at the standard rate of 24% . The local tax authority conducts periodic and ad hoc tax filing reviews on business enterprises after those enterprises complete their relevant tax filings. Therefore, the Company’s tax filings are subject to examination. It is therefore uncertain as to whether the local tax authority may take different views about the Company’s tax filings, which may lead to additional tax liabilities. As of March 31, 2026 and 2025, all of the Company’s tax returns remain open for statutory examination by relevant tax authorities. Conwall Malaysia evaluates its uncertain tax positions in accordance with applicable accounting guidance. The Company recognizes interest and penalties related to uncertain tax positions, if any, as a component of income tax expense. As of March 31, 2026, the Company did not have any significant uncertain tax positions requiring recognition or disclosure in the accompanying consolidated financial statements. F- 57 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Service taxes Service tax is a consumption tax levied by Malaysian tax authorities and is charged on any taxable service income provided in Malaysia by a registered company in carrying on their business. Conwall Malaysia is engaged in the business of construction services, which became subject to certain construction-related service tax on July 1, 2025. Conwall registered with the local tax authorities in August 2025 and commenced filing service tax returns and remitting service tax beginning in September 2025. For construction-related services, the applicable service tax rates are 6 % ad valorem for construction work and 8 % ad valorem for maintenance or repair work. A company is required to register for service tax purposes if the total value of its taxable services over a rolling 12-month period exceeds, or is expected to exceed, the prescribed registration threshold of $ 370,627 (RM 1,500,000 ) for construction service providers. Service tax collected is not an expense of the Company and is recorded as a liability until remitted to the Malaysian tax authorities. The Company presents revenue net of service tax collected. Payroll Taxes and Statutory Contributions Under Malaysian income tax regulations, employers are required to withhold employee income taxes under the Monthly Tax Deduction (“MTD”), also known as Potongan Cukai Bulanan (“PCB”), system administered by the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia. The Company withholds the required amounts from employees’ salaries and remits them to the Malaysian tax authorities on a monthly basis. As the Company acts solely as a withholding agent, amounts withheld from employees’ compensation are not recognized as an expense of the Company and are recorded as payroll tax payable until remitted. In addition to employee income tax withholdings, the Company is required to make statutory employer contributions to employee benefit programs, including the Employees Provident Fund (“EPF”), the Social Security Organization (“SOCSO”), the Employment Insurance System (“EIS”), and, where applicable, the Human Resource Development Corporation (“HRD Corp”). Employer contributions are recognized as employee benefit expense in the period in which the related services are rendered. Amounts due but not yet remitted are included in accrued payroll-related liabilities. HRD Corp administers Malaysia’s Human Resources Development Fund, which is financed through a statutory levy paid by eligible employers. Employers subject to the levy may apply for grants or reimbursements for qualifying employee training and workforce development programs. Levies paid to HRD Corp are recognized as employee benefit expense, while reimbursements received for approved training programs are recognized as a reduction of the related training expense or as other operating income, as appropriate, when realization is probable. F- 58 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued) Related Parties Transactions The Company identifies related parties, and accounts for, discloses related party transactions in accordance with ASC 850, “Related Party Disclosures” and other relevant ASC standards. A related party is generally defined as (i) any person that holds 10% or more of the Company’s securities and their immediate families, (ii) the Company’s management, (iii) someone that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control with the Company, or (iv) anyone who can significantly influence the financial and operating decisions of the Company. A transaction is considered as a related party transaction when there is a transfer of resources or obligations between related parties. Related parties may be individuals or corporate entities. Transactions involving related parties cannot be presumed to be carried out on an arm’s-length basis, as the requisite conditions of competitive, free market dealings may not exist. Representations about transactions with related parties, if made, shall not imply that the related party transactions were consummated on terms equivalent to those that prevail in arm’s-length transactions unless such representations can be substantiated. It is not, however, practical to determine the fair value of amounts of related party transactions due to their related party nature. Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements In November 2024, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (“ASU”) No. 2024-03, Income Statement – Reporting Comprehensive Income – Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses, requiring public companies to disclose additional information about specific expense categories in the notes to the consolidated financial statements on an annual and interim basis. ASU No. 2024-03 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2026, and for interim periods beginning after December 15, 2027. Early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this ASU on its unaudited consolidated financial statements and related disclosures. In December 2025, the FASB issued ASU No. 2025-11, Interim Reporting (Topic 270): Narrow-Scope Improvements, which clarifies the guidance in Topic 270 to improve the consistency of interim financial reporting. The ASU provides a comprehensive list of required interim disclosures and introduces a disclosure principle requiring entities to disclose events since the end of the last annual reporting period that have a material impact on the entity. ASU No. 2025-11 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2027, including interim periods within those fiscal years, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this ASU on its unaudited interim consolidated financial statements and related disclosures. F- 64 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 9- INVOICE FINANCING LIABILITIES The Company participates in accounts receivable (“AR”) and accounts payable (“AP”) invoice financing arrangements with financial institutions to manage working capital and enhance liquidity. (1) Accounts Receivable Invoice Financing Accounts receivable invoice financing is an arrangement under which the Company pledges eligible trade receivables as collateral to obtain short-term financing from financial institutions prior to customer collection. The Company retains ownership of the underlying receivables and continues to recognize such receivables in its consolidated balance sheets. Accordingly, the arrangement is accounted for as a secured borrowing. In November 2025, the Company pledged accounts receivable with a carrying amount of $ 11,118,798 (RM 45,000,000 ) as collateral to obtain a 27-day loan of $ 4,941,688 (RM 20,000,000 ). The financing bore interest at an annual rate of 4.6 %, and the Company incurred interest expense of $ 16,347 (RM 68,055 ). The loan was repaid in full upon its maturity in December 2025, and the related customer collections were received during the same period. Accordingly, as of March 31, 2026, the Company had no outstanding accounts receivable invoice financing arrangements. For the year ended March 31, 2026, the Company recognized $ 16,347 (RM 68,055 ) of interest expense related to accounts receivable invoice financing. The Company’s accounts receivable invoice financing arrangement is accounted for as a secured borrowing. Accordingly, cash proceeds received from the financing arrangement and repayments of principal are presented as cash flows from financing activities in the consolidated statements of cash flows. Cash collections of the underlying trade accounts receivable are presented as operating activities, consistent with the Company’s normal cash receipts for accounts receivable from customers. Interest paid is included in cash flows from operating activities. (2) Accounts Payable invoice financing Accounts payable invoice financing is a supplier finance arrangement under which a financial institution settles eligible supplier invoices on behalf of the Company, and the Company repays the financial institution at a later date in accordance with the agreed terms. Beginning in August 2025, the Company entered into an Account Payable invoice financing arrangement with a financial institution to facilitate settlement of eligible supplier invoices. Under the arrangement, the Company may obtain financing of up to $ 9,883,376 (RM 40,000,000 ) in outstanding principal at any time, with individual financing terms of up to 90 days. Amounts financed bear interest at a rate of 1.5 % per annum above the financial institution’s prevailing Effective Cost of Funds. Accordingly, the effective interest rate fluctuates based on changes in the underlying benchmark rate. The repayment obligations under the Account Payable invoice financing facility are guaranteed by the directors of Conwall Construction Industries Sdn. Bhd., Mr. Hu Jingji and Mr. Ng Boon Teik, up to the maximum facility amount of $ 9,883,376 (RM 40,000,000 ). F- 65 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 9- INVOICE FINANCING LIABILITIES (continued) (2) Accounts Payable invoice financing (continued) From time to time, the Company submits eligible supplier invoices to the financial institution, which pays the suppliers directly on the Company’s behalf. Upon payment by the financial institution, the Company’s obligation to the supplier is satisfied and a corresponding obligation to the financial institution is recognized. The Company subsequently repays the financial institution at maturity or earlier, together with accrued interest and bank charges. Upon repayment of the outstanding financing, the Company may submit additional eligible supplier invoices to the financial institution for financing, provided that the aggregate outstanding financing balance does not exceed the maximum financing facility of $ 9,883,376 (RM 40,000,000 ). The Company accounts for the arrangement as a financing obligation. Accordingly, amounts outstanding under the arrangement are presented separately from trade accounts payable in the consolidated balance sheets as Invoice Financing Liabilities. At the time the financial institution settles eligible supplier invoices on the Company’s behalf, the payments made directly to the suppliers are considered non-cash financing activities and, accordingly, are excluded from changes in accounts payable in the consolidated statements of cash flows. Subsequent repayments of principal to the financial institution are presented as cash flows from financing activities, while interest paid is presented as cash flows from operating activities. In the year ended March 31, 2026, the Company recognized $ 73,967 (RM 307,932 ) of interest expense related to the accounts payable invoice financing arrangement. The effective interest rate applicable to amounts financed under the arrangements ranged from 4.60 % to 4.88 % per annum. As of March 31, 2026, the outstanding balance under the arrangement was $ 1,711,459 (RM 6,926,617 ). F- 66 CONWALL CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES LIMITED AND SUBSIDIARY NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS Note 10- BANK LOAN - MULTI-OPTION LOAN In August 2025, the Company had a Multi-Option Loan (“MOL”) facility with a financial institution providing a maximum principal amount of $ 6,385,069 (RM 26,600,000 ) to finance the acquisition of the manufacturing facility, as more fully described in Note 4 – Property, Plant and Equipment. In October 2025, the Company drew $ 5,164,064 (RM 20,900,000 ) under the facility to fund a portion of the purchase price of the manufacturing facility, with the loan proceeds disbursed directly by the lending institution to the seller. The Company intends to utilize the remaining available loan proceeds of $ 1,408,381 (RM 5,700,000 ) to finance the balance of the purchase price, subject to the terms and conditions of the loan facility. The loan facility is guaranteed by the directors of Conwall Malaysia, Mr. Hu Jingji and Mr. Ng Boon Teik. The loan bears interest at a variable rate equal to 1.50 % per annum above the lending institution’s prevailing one-month Effective Cost of Funds, with interest calculated on monthly rests. Accordingly, the interest rate fluctuates with changes in the underlying benchmark rate. The loan is repayable over a period of 54 months. The Company is required to make 53 monthly installments of $ 37,804 (RM 153,000 ), each consisting of principal and accrued interest, followed by payment of the remaining outstanding principal together with any accrued interest in the 54th month. Interest is payable monthly in arrears. The financial institution will review the facility prior to maturity to determine whether to renew or extend the remaining amortization period beyond the initial 54-month term, subject to satisfactory account performance, the Company’s financial condition, and the continued satisfaction of the financial institution’s credit requirements. However, the financial institution is under no obligation to renew or extend the facility. The loan may not be prepaid without the prior written consent of the financial institution. If prepayment is approved, the Company may be required to pay a prepayment fee equal to 2.0 % of the amount prepaid, together with any funding losses incurred by the financial institution as a result of the prepayment. The Company paid interest of $ 39,788 (RM 165,643 ) in the three months ended December 31, 2025. The Company commenced making monthly installment of $ 37,804 (RM 153,000 ) in January 2026. For the year ended March 31, 2026, the Company recognized interest expense of $ 111,915 (RM 465,915 ) related to the loan, and the effective interest rate ranged from 4.15 % to 5.05 %. As of March 31, 2026, the outstanding principal balance of the loan was $ 5,107,926 (RM 20,672,797 ). As disclosed in Note 15 – Subsequent Events, the Company drew loan proceeds of $ 469,460 (RM 1,900,000 ) in April 2026 and an additional $ 469,460 (RM 1,900,000 ) in May 2026, for total additional borrowings of $ 938,920 (RM 3,800,000 ). In May 2026, the financial institution revised the repayment schedule and notified the Company that, effective May 2026, the required monthly installment would be $ 37,804 (RM 153,000 ) plus accrued interest. Liquidity risk The Company is exposed to liquidity risk which is risk that it is unable to provide sufficient capital resources and liquidity to meet its commitments and business needs. When necessary, the Company will turn to other financial institutions and the shareholders to obtain short-term funding to meet the liquidity shortage. Other risk The Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations may also be negatively impacted by risks related to natural disasters, extreme weather conditions, health epidemics and other catastrophic incidents, such as the COVID-19 outbreak and spread, which could significantly disrupt the Company’s operations.
